learning_outcomes.text: Basic knowledge about the use and programming of computers, operating systems, databases, and computer programs with application in engineering.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.

Permanent self-learning. Use learning continuously and develop autonomous and flexible learning strategies throughout life to be part of an active, motivated, and integrated citizenry, favoring job improvement or personal development.
Knows and fluently uses tools to retrieve information from digital sources (including browsers, search engines, and catalogs).
Knows the basic operation of computers, operating systems, and databases, and creates simple programs on them.
Uses computer equipment effectively, considering its logical and physical properties.
Knows and uses environments for program development.
Analyzes and generates solutions to information processing problems in the world of engineering of low-medium complexity.

syllabus_topics: Introduction. Computer structure and functions. Computer hardware. Introduction to Operating Systems, application software of interest for the degree. Programming languages, compilers, and interpreters.
Basic data types, operators, and expressions. Data input and output (screen).
Control structures. Sequential, conditional, and iterative composition. Procedures and functions.
Compound data types. Data structures. Vectors and matrices. Strings.
Text files. Files with character-delimited data.
assessment_rules: The overall grade is calculated from a written exam (P1) and a practical part (P2). P1 accounts for 80% of the grade, with a minimum score of 5 out of 10 required. P2 accounts for 20% of the grade, provided the minimum in P1 is met. For the first call, P2 can be achieved through assignments (P2A) or a global practical exam (P2B); for the second call, P2 can only be achieved through P2B. Non-attendance to the written exam in the first call, or to both the written and global practical exams in the second call, will result in a 'not presented' status. Students must be able to demonstrate authorship of all evaluated work through an oral interview, otherwise, the grade for that activity will be zero.
